issues.legal_issue: A conditional building-plan approval does not create an enforceable right before the required land conversion and payment are completed and final approval is granted.
material_facts: The plans were submitted before the later building restrictions took effect.
The Board made any effectiveness of the plans conditional on converting the land to freehold and paying the conversion charges.
The applicants had not completed the required conversion and payments, and no final sanction had been granted to the plans.
issues.conclusion: The applicants acquired no legal right in respect of the plans before conversion was completed and the plans were finally sanctioned.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 179 and 181 of the Cantonments Act, 1924, a plan is not sanctioned merely because it has been submitted or conditionally considered. The High Court’s decision in W.P. Nos. 2236 and 2237 of 1983, dated 15 April 1987, was followed: completion of the conversion formalities and payment were conditions precedent to sanction.

rule.if: building_plan_approval_dispute and plan_effectiveness_conditioned_on_land_conversion_and_payment and required_conversion_or_payment_incomplete and final_plan_sanction_absent

predicates.building_plan_approval_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether an applicant has a right to build under a submitted building plan.
predicates.plan_effectiveness_conditioned_on_land_c: The approving authority made the plan’s effectiveness depend on completing a land-tenure conversion and paying the required charges.
predicates.required_conversion_or_payment_incomplet: The applicant had not completed the required conversion or payments.
predicates.final_plan_sanction_absent: The approving authority had not granted final sanction to the plan.

issues.definition: When a building-plan dispute involves a plan conditional on conversion and payment, and those requirements remain incomplete without final sanction, the applicant has no enforceable right under the plan before final sanction.

issues.legal_issue: A building plan must be considered under the building regulations in force when it is sanctioned, rather than regulations that have ceased to apply.
material_facts: The applicants relied on plans submitted before the first scheme of restrictions was introduced.
The plans had not been finally sanctioned, and the applicants had not submitted fresh plans conforming to the intervening schemes.
The earlier bye-laws were superseded, and the 1988 bye-laws were in force when any fresh plans would be considered.
issues.conclusion: Any fresh plans submitted by the applicants had to be governed by the building regulations in force when those plans were considered for sanction.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Sections 181(2) and 181A of the Cantonments Act, 1924, concerning schemes of building restrictions, and Sections 186 and 283 concerning bye-laws. It held that the 1988 bye-laws superseded the earlier bye-laws and that a plan is governed by the regulations prevailing at the time of sanction.

predicates.building_plan_approval_dispute: The proceeding concerns which building regulations govern approval of a building plan.
predicates.plan_not_finally_sanctioned: The plan had not received final sanction.
predicates.building_regulations_changed_before_sanc: The applicable building regulations changed before the plan was sanctioned.

issues.definition: If a plan remains unsanctioned when building regulations change, the plan is governed by the regulations in force when sanction is considered.

issues.legal_issue: Private interests in maximizing building space are subordinate to building restrictions adopted for the broader needs of urban residents.
material_facts: The schemes restricted floor space, open space, building height, and the number of storeys.
The restrictions were introduced to address overcrowding and haphazard high-rise construction and to account for environmental, sanitation, and basic-amenity concerns.
The applicants sought to rely on earlier plans to pursue construction under less restrictive rules; the validity of the schemes and bye-laws was not challenged before the Court.
issues.conclusion: The building restrictions, made in the larger public interest, prevailed over the applicants’ interest in maximizing construction.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Sections 181(2) and 181A of the Cantonments Act, 1924, for the schemes and Sections 186 and 283 for the bye-laws. It emphasized that building controls addressing overcrowding, environmental hazards, sanitation, and essential amenities serve the interests of the whole population and are not displaced by private demands for greater building area.

predicates.building_restriction_dispute: The proceeding concerns the application of restrictions on building construction.
predicates.restrictions_address_overcrowding_or_urb: The restrictions were adopted to address overcrowding or protect urban amenities and residents.
predicates.applicant_seeks_maximum_building_space: The applicant sought to maximize the area or scale of construction.

issues.definition: When restrictions address overcrowding or urban amenities and an applicant seeks maximum building space, the restrictions prevail over that private interest.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier order that expressly leaves the merits undecided does not establish a precedent on the merits of the same disputed issue.
material_facts: The applicants relied on an earlier appellate order that had allowed construction subject to specified restrictions.
That order expressly stated that it expressed no opinion on the parties’ contentions or the questions decided by the High Court and addressed the disposition of the earlier parties’ proceedings.
The applicants invoked that order as support for their own claims.
issues.conclusion: The earlier order was not a precedent on the disputed questions and did not support the applicants’ claims.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished Shoriar Baharam Irani & Ors. v. Pune Cantonment Board & Ors., Civil Appeal No. 2184 of 1987, order dated 23 February 1990, because that order expressly disclaimed any opinion on the merits or the questions decided by the High Court.

predicates.building_restriction_dispute: The proceeding concerns the merits of a dispute over building restrictions.
predicates.earlier_order_expressly_reserved_merits: An earlier order expressly stated that it did not decide the merits of the relevant contentions or issues.
predicates.earlier_order_limited_to_its_parties: The earlier order disposed of the proceedings of the parties before it without determining the issue for other cases.

issues.definition: An earlier order that reserves the merits and is confined to the proceedings before it is not precedent on those reserved merits.
